strengths: FALCON addresses a relevant problem: retaining previous segmentation classes while learning imbalanced new classes and distinguishing future classes hidden in the background. Combining prototype retention with learned assignment to multiple unknown clusters is a useful direction.

The empirical evaluation is substantial, covering ADE20K, Pascal VOC, and Cityscapes with several incremental schedules and both convolutional and transformer models. Reported gains include 36.4 versus 34.9 mIoU for the strongest listed DeepLab-V3 comparator on ADE20K 100-10, and 62.41 versus 59.25 on VOC 10-1 (Tables 5–6).

Table 1 provides concrete evidence of improved minority-class performance. On ADE20K 100-50, the proposed loss increases minority mIoU from 26.4 to 30.8 while improving majority mIoU from 51.5 to 52.1, narrowing the group gap without sacrificing majority performance.

The fixed-versus-adaptive visual grammar comparison supports updating the assignment model during continual learning: ADE20K 100-50 improves from 35.6 to 37.9 mIoU (Table 2). Additional ablations examine the scaling factor, cluster margin, neighborhood size, and backbone. The appendix supplies useful implementation details and a procedural overview.
weaknesses: The central fairness argument does not establish its claimed geometric interpretation. Propositions 1–2 concern normalized probability mass over samples; a smaller value of this probability does not imply tighter feature clusters. Features can change arbitrarily in directions orthogonal to a centroid without changing their dot products with it. Consequently, the probability equalization argument does not demonstrate minority-cluster compactness or explain the observed fairness improvements.

The loss definition and optimization contain material ambiguities. Proposition 2 requires the transition vector v to participate in the normalization, but Eq. (4) retains a denominator defined over image features. If v is excluded and unconstrained, its loss term is unbounded below. Also, Eq. (8) optimizes segmentation parameters while the cluster regularizer depends only on centroids, which are described as momentum-updated and fixed during loss computation. Under those updates, the regularizer has no gradient to the segmentation model; the mechanism producing its gains in Table 4 is unspecified.

The knowledge-distillation justification in Appendix Section 4 is not valid for the proposed contrastive loss. Equation (16) invokes a metric triangle inequality and then identifies its terms with the contrastive objective, which is not shown to be a metric. The subsequent Big-O argument therefore does not establish that minimizing this objective preserves the distillation constraint.

The unknown-class ablations do not cleanly isolate the attention model. Section 4.2 states that removing visual grammar also reduces the number of unknown clusters to one. Thus, improvements combine learned assignment with increased representational capacity for unknown classes. A comparison using the same multiple clusters and a simpler assignment rule is missing. Figure 6 is suggestive, but provides no quantitative assessment of unknown-cluster quality.

The experiments establish improved group-average accuracy more clearly than the specific proposed fairness mechanism. Table 1 changes both the scaling factor and the transition-vector term; it lacks a correspondingly rescaled vanilla-loss control. Comparisons against simpler class-balancing objectives are also absent, and the exact majority/minority partition is insufficiently documented. This limits attribution of the gains to the claimed mechanism.

Important reproduction details remain missing, including DBSCAN parameters, selection of unknown pixels from the mixed background, resolution of multiple cluster assignments, and the visual grammar pretraining and training schedules. Computational measurements are also absent despite the efficiency framing and additional clustering and transformer training. Together with the unresolved objective and theoretical issues, these gaps outweigh the substantial empirical merits and determine the weak-reject recommendation.
